one_line_contribution: A same-stream, paired-probe measurement claiming that an in-context experience bank and a continual-LoRA parametric store fail on opposite sides of a mid-stream rule change — the bank drags forward on post-shift tasks in proportion to the fraction of retrieved items that are pre-shift (and recovers on a schedule computable from bank composition alone), while the LoRA instead loses pre-shift competence in proportion to post-shift update count unless replay is paid.
closest_prior_work: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams (arXiv:2607.26017, verified to exist via the literature command, S2 record 2026-07-28, cit 0). Its own framing is the proposal's thesis: complementary episodic storage versus gradual consolidation as the plasticity/stability split, evaluated on boundary-agnostic task streams. I could NOT verify its contents — S2 returns only a TLDR and HF has no abstract — so I cannot say whether it contains the per-substrate failure-side analysis or only a routing system with end-task numbers. The proposal flags exactly this and is honest about it, but an unresolved abstract on the single closest system is a live risk, not a cleared one. Second threat: Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget? (arXiv:2605.09315, verified, cit 4), which already documents capability degradation across BOTH the memory channel and the model channel and supplies CPE as the fix; the proposal's delta over it is 'same stream, matched preservation cost,' which is a control condition rather than a new phenomenon. Third: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs (arXiv:2605.12978, verified, cit 10) already reports the asymmetry that consolidated memory degrades while a raw-episodic control holds up — the same directional result with LLM consolidation standing in for weights. Fourth, on the in-context half: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents (arXiv:2608.07622, which I verified exists — the proposal's own collision check did not) and The Compliance Trap (arXiv:2607.10608, verified), which already establishes that conflicting retrieved memory produces compounding errors and weak recovery. Also worth naming as a conceptual precedent, though not a collision: arXiv:2607.19749, 'The World Model Remembers, the Actor Forgets,' which is the identical opposite-sided template in continual model-based RL.
strongest_objection: Two objections, both fatal as written. (1) The headline is largely definitional, and the proposal says so itself: 'a bank forgets nothing and a LoRA retrieves nothing.' An append-only, never-evicted bank cannot lose phase-1 competence because it still literally contains every phase-1 item; a LoRA trained only on phase-2 successes under a grammar that renames the actions cannot retain the phase-1 mapping without replay. P3 therefore passes by construction under S1, and 'opposite-sided failure' is a restatement of the two substrates' storage semantics rather than an empirical discovery. Worse, the parametric side conflates 'capability eroded' with 'a surface action-name mapping was correctly overwritten' — there is no probe of any capability the shift did not relabel (off-stream ALFWorld competence, or a non-ALFWorld held-out set), so the plan cannot tell the two apart, which is precisely the distinction CapTrack (2603.06610) and CPE (2605.09315) already draw. (2) P1's statistics do not support its claim. Stale fraction is a deterministic function of bank composition, and at a given probe point every episode draws from the same bank, so stale fraction barely varies within a probe point and is near-collinear with time-since-shift and bank size. The 'probe-level logistic regression of failure on stale fraction' therefore has an effective N of about 12 probe points x 2 seeds per condition, not the tens of thousands of episodes implied; if episodes are pooled as independent the CI is anticonservative, and either way a positive coefficient is produced by any monotone recovery over time regardless of whether staleness is the mechanism. The bank-composition 'predictor' in P2 compounds this: with an append-every-episode store and a 200/200/200 phase design, the probe point at which the median retrieval set becomes majority post-shift is fixed by arithmetic, and the tolerance is +/-50 episodes inside a 200-episode phase. That is a counting argument with a wide window, not a model, and it succeeds unless the retriever turns out to be phase-discriminative — which the proposal's own risk section says is likely for S1, where post-shift trajectories are textually distinguishable. A reviewer will also note the internal inconsistency in the noise section: the stated per-window MDE is 4-5 points, yet the equivalence bounds in P1, P3 and P4 are all 3 points, so every predicted null is underpowered by construction while the text asserts 'all thresholds sit at or above' the MDE.
what_would_fix_it: Replace the observational stale-fraction regression with a randomized within-probe-point dose ladder: at a fixed probe point, fixed k and fixed token count, force retrieval sets containing 0/1/2/3 pre-shift items and measure failure across the ladder. That makes P1 a manipulation rather than a time-series correlation, removes the collinearity with probe index and bank size, and removes the confound the program's own pilot already identified (that injection volume, not content, is the causal lever — which the k=1/k=7 ablation reintroduces). Make the two sides symmetric: add a bounded, evicting bank (FIFO or capacity-capped, as every deployed store is) and a PM-reset arm (fresh LoRA at each boundary) so that IC-reset is not the only oracle; the bank's immunity to erosion should be shown to survive eviction rather than being granted by an unbounded store. Add an off-stream capability probe on tasks the shift does not touch so parametric 'erosion' is separated from correct overwriting of a relabeled grammar, and make S2 (the procedure shift, where old trajectories are semantically rather than syntactically wrong) a budgeted primary condition instead of 'an extension,' since S1 alone cannot distinguish these. Finally, recompute the MDE and either raise the equivalence bounds above it or enlarge probe sets and seeds (2 seeds is thin for a Spearman-rho monotonicity claim in a program that has already watched noise swallow claims), and resolve the UniMem abstract before claiming the opposite-sided characterization is first.
missing_baseline: A bounded, evicting in-context bank (size-capped or FIFO/utility-evicted, e.g. 100-200 items) run on the same stream. Every IC arm here is append-only and unbounded, which hands the proposal its own headline: the bank retains phase-1 competence because no phase-1 item is ever removed. With eviction, the in-context substrate erodes on the pre-shift side too and the 'opposite-sided' claim may collapse to 'both erode, one faster.' Secondary omission: PM-reset (re-initialized LoRA at each phase boundary) as the parametric analogue of IC-reset, so both substrates get their oracle fix and the preservation-cost comparison in P6 is symmetric.

LoRA continual fine-tuning versus retrieval bank probe' returned only three papers (2605.05413, 2604.20572, 2603.11653) and is reported as empty of collisions, not as evidence of novelty. Q6: 'Controlled Memory Interference' returned and verified 2608.07622 (2026-08-07, cit 1). arXiv IDs I verified via the literature command: 2607.26017, 2604.27003, 2605.09315, 2606.04703, 2605.12978, 2606.02461, 2601.03192, 2608.07622, plus 2607.10608 and 2602.04288 through HF records. I could NOT verify the substance of 2607.26017 (TLDR only, no abstract on either channel) — this is the one ID the novelty argument actually leans on, and it remains unresolved. Judging the proposal's own check: it is well above average — five queries, IDs listed, an explicit statement of which abstracts were unreachable, and an honest self-flag of UniMem as residual risk. Two demerits: it cites 2608.07622 in Related Work without having verified it (I did), and it treats an unreadable abstract on the single closest system as a limitation rather than as a reason to withhold the 'first opposite-sided characterization' claim in the abstract.
